tokyo_gusuku.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own site — starters, chanpuru, goat dishes, fried items, single plates, rice and noodles, and the drinks list including the awamori bottles. 新宿区新宿3-8-5 中川ビル2F, 19:00–02:00, open every day, one minute from Shinjuku-sanchome C4; the shop states an average spend of about ¥7,000. Tabelog is UNVERIFIED rather than empty: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ON THIS RECORD, AND ONE OF THE SHARPEST TRAPS IN THE WHOLE DATASET: 沖縄そば CONTAINS NO BUCKWHEAT AT ALL. It is made from 100% WHEAT flour, and it is permitted to keep the word そば only by a specific exemption negotiated with Japan’s fair-trade authorities — every other noodle sold as そば must contain at least 30% buckwheat. So a coeliac who has learned to be wary of soba for the usual reason (二八, 打ち粉, shared water) will still be wrong here, and wrong in the opposite direction: this is not soba with some wheat in it, it is a wheat noodle wearing the name. It appears twice on this menu, as a bowl and as ゴーヤめし’s companion. ⚠ THE SECOND TRAP IS 麸 AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY. フーチャンプルー is built on 麸 — FU, which is pure WHEAT GLUTEN, the most concentrated wheat product in Japanese cooking — and yet fu is entirely plant-based, so a vegan scanning for a tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry may land on precisely the dish a coeliac must avoid most. The two diets fail on opposite halves of this menu repeatedly. ⚠ AND ソーミンチャンプルー IS SOMEN: wheat noodles, stir-fried. Three of the nine noodle-or-gluten items here hide their wheat behind an Okinawan word. ⚠ WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD HERE, AND IT IS MORE THAN MOST: ジーマミ豆腐 is not tofu at all but PEANUT and sweet-potato starch — no soy, no wheat, no dashi, and a nut allergen instead. 豆腐よう is island tofu fermented in 紅麹 and AWAMORI, which is rice-based. スヌイ is Okinawan mozuku seaweed. ゴーヤ刺し is raw bitter melon. And the awamori list matters for a coeliac beyond this shop: awamori is distilled from long-grain RICE with black koji and never from barley, which makes it the one Japanese spirit category with no grain question at all — unlike 麦焼酎, and unlike whisky. ⚠ ONE ITEM IS A DELIBERATE-LOOKING VEGAN TRAP: スク豆腐 is chilled island tofu with スク on top — salted juvenile RABBITFISH. A tofu dish that is a fish dish, with nothing in the Japanese name to say so unless you know the word.

items.ja: 油みそときゅうり
items.note: ⚠ 油みそ / アンダンスー IS NOT A VEGETABLE DIP. It is MISO cooked down with PORK BELLY and fat — the cucumber is the vehicle. Miso is also frequently 麦味噌, barley.

items.ja: ミミガー（酢みそ）
items.note: Sliced pig ear cartilage. The 酢みそ dressing is miso and vinegar, and miso is fermented on koji that is often barley.

items.ja: 梅クラゲときゅうり
items.note: Jellyfish is animal; a ume dressing is normally soy-based.

items.ja: 豆腐よう
items.note: ⚠ A REAL FIND, AND WORTH KNOWING WHAT IT IS: island tofu fermented for months in 紅麹 red koji and AWAMORI, eaten in tiny slivers like a cheese. Soybeans, rice koji and rice spirit — nothing animal at any point, and no wheat unless the koji is a barley one, which for tofuyo it traditionally is not. One of the few Japanese fermented delicacies that reaches a vegan.

items.ja: ジーマミ豆腐
items.note: ⚠ IT IS NOT TOFU AND IT IS NOT SOY. ジーマミ is Okinawan for PEANUT: this is peanut milk set with sweet-potato starch, which makes it naturally free of wheat and of anything animal — and a NUT dish, which matters more here than either diet flag. The gluten question is only the sauce poured over it, which is normally a soy-based one; ask for it plain.

items.ja: 島豆腐やっこ
items.note: Island tofu is firmer and saltier than mainland tofu, coagulated with seawater. Plant in itself; it arrives with soy sauce, and chilled tofu in Japan very often carries a pinch of KATSUOBUSHI as a garnish nobody mentions.

items.ja: ゴーヤチャンプルー
items.note: The signature Okinawan stir-fry: bitter melon, island tofu, pork and egg. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: フーチャンプルー
items.note: ⚠ THE MOST CONCENTRATED WHEAT ITEM ON THIS MENU AND IT LOOKS LIKE THE VEGETARIAN ONE. 麸 (fu) is PURE WHEAT GLUTEN — flour washed until only the protein remains — so this dish is closer to eating gluten neat than any noodle is. It is also entirely plant-based in itself, which is exactly the problem: a vegan scanning an Okinawan menu for a tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry can land on the single worst dish here for a coeliac. As cooked, it carries egg and pork anyway. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: 豆腐チャンプルー
items.note: Island tofu with vegetables. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: ミミガーチャンプルー
items.note: Pig ear. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: ポークチャンプルー
items.note: ポーク in Okinawa means canned LUNCHEON MEAT — SPAM — not fresh pork. Processed meat of that kind commonly carries wheat-derived starch as a binder on top of the soy seasoning. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: ソーミンチャンプルー
items.note: ⚠ ソーミン IS 素麺 — thin WHEAT noodles, stir-fried rather than served in broth. The Okinawan spelling hides an ordinary wheat noodle. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: イカ墨チャンプルー
items.note: Squid and its ink. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: 中味チャンプルー
items.note: 中味 is pig INNARDS. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: チキナーチャンプルー
items.note: チキナー is Okinawan pickled mustard greens — plant, and stir-fried with pork and egg like the rest. ⚠ チャンプルー IS A STIR-FRY OF TOFU WITH EGG AND PORK, seasoned with soy — the format itself is neither vegan nor wheat-free before any specific ingredient is considered.

items.ja: 人参しりしり
items.note: Grated carrot stir-fried with EGG — one of the simplest dishes here and one of the few with no obvious wheat, though it is normally seasoned with dashi and a splash of soy.

items.ja: コンビーフ野菜炒め
items.note: Canned corned beef with vegetables; soy-seasoned.

items.ja: ヒージャー刺し
items.note: ⚠ The shop’s speciality section, sourced 南城市 食肉センター 直送. Raw GOAT, eaten with soy and ginger — the meat carries no wheat and the dip does. The three goat dishes are the most expensive things on the menu.

items.ja: ヒージャー汁
items.note: The traditional Okinawan goat soup, seasoned with salt and ヨモギ mugwort rather than miso in its classic form — worth asking, since the seasoning decides it. Goat.

items.ja: ヒージャーおじや
items.note: Rice simmered in the goat broth.

items.ja: 紅芋コロッケ
items.note: ⚠ A KOROKKE IS CRUMBED IN PANKO — the purple sweet potato inside is plant and the shell is wheat. Croquette binder is normally milk and egg too.

items.ja: 田芋コロッケ
items.note: Okinawan taro in a panko shell.

items.ja: 島豆腐厚揚げ
items.note: Deep-fried island tofu — plant in itself, and the best-looking vegan prospect in this section. Two things stop it: it comes out of the same fryer as the panko croquettes above, and atsuage is normally served with soy sauce and very often a scattering of KATSUOBUSHI.

items.ja: スヌイ沖縄県産もずく
items.note: ⚠ ONE OF THE BEST VEGAN ITEMS HERE. スヌイ is the Okinawan word for mozuku, a fine seaweed harvested in the islands — plant, and nothing else in the bowl. The gluten flag is against only because mozuku is served in 三杯酢, a vinegar dressing built on SOY SAUCE and usually dashi; ask for it with plain vinegar and it clears both.

items.ja: スク豆腐
items.en: Island tofu topped with salted juvenile rabbitfish
items.note: ⚠ THE PUREST VEGAN TRAP ON THIS MENU. It reads as a tofu dish and the whole point of it is the スク — salted juvenile RABBITFISH, laid across the top. Nothing in the name says fish unless you already know the Okinawan word, and the fish is the dish rather than a garnish. Soy sauce as well.

items.ja: ラフテイ（豚角煮）
items.note: Pork belly simmered for hours in AWAMORI, soy sauce and brown sugar. The soy is dissolved through the meat, so there is no plain version.

items.ja: テビチ（豚足煮込）
items.note: Pig trotters, soy-simmered.

items.ja: ポーク玉子
items.note: SPAM and fried egg — the Okinawan staple. Luncheon meat commonly carries wheat starch as a binder, which is the open question.

items.ja: ポークかりかり焼き
items.note: SPAM, fried crisp.

items.ja: ゴーヤ刺し
items.note: ⚠ ONE OF VERY FEW HOT-KITCHEN-FREE PLANT DISHES IN THIS DATASET: raw bitter melon, sliced. No stir-fry, no egg, no pork, no fryer. The gluten flag is a question only because 刺し in Japan means "with soy sauce" by default — ask for salt instead.

items.ja: スーチカ 豚塩漬
items.note: ⚠ WORTH NOTING FOR THE METHOD: スーチカー is pork preserved in SALT rather than soy, which is unusual on a Japanese board and removes the obvious wheat route. Pork, and the finishing seasoning is not described.

items.ja: ポチギ 辛めの豚のソーセージ
items.note: The shop glosses it itself as 辛めの豚のソーセージ. Sausage binders and casings are the sort of thing never printed.

items.ja: チキアギ かまぼこ焼き
items.note: ⚠ A FISH CAKE IS A QUIET WHEAT ITEM. The shop glosses チキアギ as かまぼこ焼き — surimi, which in Japan is routinely bulked with WHEAT STARCH or flour — and it is deep-fried on top of that.

items.ja: ヒラヤーチ 沖縄風お好み焼き
items.note: ⚠ The shop translates it itself: 沖縄風お好み焼き. A hirayachi is a thin batter of WHEAT FLOUR, egg and dashi with chives — flour is the substance of the dish, and the dashi is a second problem.

items.ja: イカ墨ヒラヤーチ
items.note: Wheat batter tinted with squid ink.

items.ja: ポーポー 黒糖で作ったクレープ
items.note: The shop glosses it as a 黒糖 crêpe. A crêpe is WHEAT FLOUR; Okinawan brown sugar is plant, and whether egg or milk is in the batter is not stated.

items.ja: 沖縄そば
items.note: ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE LINE ON THIS RECORD: OKINAWA SOBA CONTAINS NO BUCKWHEAT WHATSOEVER. It is 100% WHEAT flour, kneaded with lye water, and it keeps the word そば only through a specific exemption from Japan’s labelling rules — every other product sold as そば must be at least 30% buckwheat. A coeliac who has learned that soba is risky because of 二八 blends and shared 打ち粉 will still get this one wrong, because there is no buckwheat to dilute: it is a wheat noodle with a soba name. The broth is pork and katsuo, and it is topped with 三枚肉 simmered in soy.

items.ja: やきそば（ソース／しょうゆ／けちゃっぷ／イカスミ）
items.note: ⚠ ALSO NOT BUCKWHEAT. Yakisoba noodles are WHEAT, and the shop offers four sauces of which three are wheat routes in their own right: ソース is a Worcester-style sauce, しょうゆ is soy, and ケチャップ is the only one that is not. Squid ink is the fourth.

items.ja: ゴーヤ飯
items.note: Rice cooked or fried with bitter melon — the rice is clean, but a ゴーヤめし in an Okinawan kitchen normally includes pork or luncheon meat and is soy-seasoned.

items.ja: オリオン生ビール
items.note: Okinawa’s own beer, and BEER IS BARLEY MALT — gluten from the grain itself. The only beer on the list.

items.ja: シークワーサーサワー
items.note: Okinawan citrus with shochu and soda; the base spirit is not named.

items.ja: グァバサワー
items.note: Guava, shochu and soda.

items.ja: マンゴサワー
items.note: Mango, shochu and soda.

items.ja: さんぴんハイ
items.note: さんぴん茶 is the Okinawan name for jasmine tea, cut with shochu. Base spirit unnamed.

items.ja: うっちんハイ
items.note: うっちん is Okinawan for TURMERIC — a turmeric infusion with shochu, drunk locally as a hangover measure. Base spirit unnamed.

items.ja: 菊の露ブラウン
items.price: ボトル 5,000円 / グラス 700円
items.note: ⚠ AWAMORI IS THE CLEANEST SPIRIT CATEGORY IN JAPAN FOR A COELIAC, and it is worth understanding why rather than just noting it. Awamori is distilled from long-grain INDICA RICE using BLACK KOJI (黒麹) — rice and rice only, never barley, unlike 麦焼酎 and unlike whisky, and unlike the soba shochu recorded elsewhere in this dataset whose koji is often barley. There is no grain question to ask about any bottle on this list.

items.ja: 菊の露VIP5年（30度）
items.note: Aged awamori — rice and black koji.

items.ja: 菊の露VIP8年（30度）
items.note: Aged awamori; the most expensive bottle listed.

items.ja: 瑞穂マイルド（25度）
items.note: Awamori.

items.ja: 瑞穂マイルド（35度）
items.note: Awamori at higher proof.

tokyo_texmex_factory_shibuya_k.price_note: Full food menu with prices, tax included, read from the shop’s own official お料理 page — starters, platillos, salads, tacos, burritos, sliders, fajitas, sides and desserts. The course, drinks and lunch pages exist and are not itemised here. 渋谷区神南1-19-3 ハイマンテン神南ビル2F, five minutes from Shibuya; 109 seats; open 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:30 on weekdays, through the day at weekends. A TABLE CHARGE of ¥330 per person applies after 15:00 on weekdays and all day at weekends. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge. ⚠ MEXICAN FOOD HAS A REPUTATION AS THE SAFE CUISINE FOR A COELIAC, BECAUSE CORN IS NOT WHEAT. That reputation is worth exactly as much as the tortilla it is built on, and THIS MENU NEVER SAYS WHICH TORTILLA IT USES. Corn tortillas and flour tortillas both appear across Tex-Mex; burritos are conventionally flour, tacos conventionally corn, and the shop’s ピンクタコス are coloured, which says nothing about the grain. Not one item description names the flour. So the single question that decides most of this board is the one to ask at the door, and no amount of reading resolves it here. ⚠ THE FRYER IS SHARED AND DEMONSTRABLY CARRIES TORTILLA: チミチャンガ is a tortilla-wrapped parcel deep-fried, and フライドチーズケーキ is a cheesecake wrapped in a large tortilla and deep-fried. If those tortillas are flour, then the chips, the shrimp fry, the jalapeño bombs and the chicken are all shared-oil problems. ⚠ THE SHOP DOES OFFER A REAL PLANT OPTION AND SAYS SO PLAINLY: ベジタブルミート, described as ダイズを主原料とした「ソイミート」— soy protein — available as a ¥490 taco, a ¥1,410 burrito and in the タコスサラダボウル. That is an explicit meat substitute rather than a dish that happens to lack meat, which is rare in this dataset. What it does not tell you is whether cheese and sour cream come with it as standard; on this menu they usually do. パクチビーンズ, ワカモレ and the vegetable fajita are the other plant routes. ⚠ AND THE ONE DISH WITH NO TORTILLA ANYWHERE NEAR IT IS SAUCED WITH SOY. The ¥4,880 メキシカン ビーフステーキ is finished with しょう油ベースのオリジナルステーキソース — a SOY SAUCE-based steak sauce, in a Mexican restaurant, stated in the shop’s own description. The steak is the obvious coeliac order here and the sauce is a Japanese wheat route that nothing about the cuisine would lead anyone to expect. Ask for it plain.

items.ja: TEXMEX NACHOS テクスメクスナチョス
items.note: The shop lists it as chips baked with cheese under sour cream sauce, chilli meat, avocado, pico de gallo and coriander. Tortilla chips are normally CORN, which is why nachos are the classic "safe" Mexican starter — but the chips are fried and this kitchen fries tortilla parcels in the same oil. Beef and dairy.

items.ja: FRESH GUACAMOLE フレッシュワカモレ
items.note: ⚠ THE BEST VEGAN PROSPECT ON THE MENU. The shop names every ingredient: tomato, onion, coriander, jalapeño and fresh avocado, mashed into a dip — no dairy, no egg, no stock. It is served with chips, which is where the only gluten question lies; ask for it with vegetables or on its own.

items.ja: QUESO FUNDIDO ケソフォンディード
items.note: The shop calls it its original cheese fondue, served with chips to dip. Dairy; the chips are the wheat question.

items.ja: CHILI CON CARNE チリコンカルネ
items.note: ⚠ THE MEAT AND BEANS ARE NOT THE PROBLEM — THE BREAD IS, AND IT IS IN THE SHOP’S OWN DESCRIPTION: バゲットと一緒にお召し上がりください, eat it with the BAGUETTE. A stewed chilli is one of the few Tex-Mex dishes with no tortilla in it at all, and this kitchen serves it with wheat bread instead. Ask whether it can come without.

items.ja: Spicy Shrimp Fry スパイシー シュリンプフライ
items.note: Soft-shell shrimp, fried, on chips with sour cream sauce and Mexican spice. Prawn and dairy; whether the shrimp is floured is not stated. Deep-fried, in oil this kitchen also uses for tortilla-wrapped items — see the chimichanga and the fried cheesecake.

items.ja: Chicken Tostadas チキントスターダ
items.note: A FRIED TORTILLA base with salsa roja, chicken and cheese. The whole dish sits on a tortilla, so it turns entirely on the corn-or-flour question. Listed separately at ¥650 in the shop’s highlights. ⚠ THE TORTILLA IS THE WHOLE QUESTION AND THIS MENU NEVER ANSWERS IT: a Mexican tortilla is either CORN, which carries no wheat, or FLOUR, which is wheat — and nothing anywhere on this page says which this kitchen uses for which item. That single unanswered question decides most of the board.
